focusKey: coverage-modals-b1-1961:No obligation versus prohibition in paired rules
explanation: Don't have to removes the duty to wear a badge; mustn't forbids lending it.

rationales.mustn't / don't have to: This reverses the rules: it bans wearing badges and makes lending optional.
rationales.don't have to / mustn't: Don't have to removes the duty to wear a badge; mustn't forbids lending it.

rationales.can't / should: This prohibits wearing a badge and recommends lending it, neither of which matches.

answer: I used to own a bookshop.
focusKey: coverage-modals-b1-1962:Used to for a former state
explanation: Used to + verb describes a former situation; here the speaker no longer owns the shop.

Am used to means ownership is familiar to you; it does not describe a situation that has ended.
This describes making use of a shop, not owning one in the past.
Used to + verb describes a former situation; here the speaker no longer owns the shop.
Would like to expresses a wish, not a former state.

sentence: 'You'd better back up those files, or you may lose your work.'

taskText: 'You'd better back up those files, or you may lose your work.'
text: Choose the meaning of the warning. 'You'd better back up those files, or you may lose your work.'
options: Backing up the files was necessary in the past.
The speaker would prefer to back up the files personally.
The listener probably backed up the files already.
Backing up the files is strongly advisable because there is a risk.
answer: Backing up the files is strongly advisable because there is a risk.
explanation: Had better gives strong advice, often with an unwanted result if it is ignored.

rationales.Backing up the files was necessary in th: Had in had better does not put this advice in the past; the action is needed now.
rationales.The speaker would prefer to back up the: You'd better addresses the listener's action; it is not the speaker's personal preference.
rationales.The listener probably backed up the file: The warning advises a future action and does not conclude that it has happened.
rationales.Backing up the files is strongly advisab: Had better gives strong advice, often with an unwanted result if it is ignored.

rationales.able to: Able needs be after will: will be able to.
rationales.be able: Able requires to before the action verb: able to handle.

rationales.be signed: The form receives the action, so use has to be + past participle: be signed.

answer: The technician managed to restart it.

Might restart leaves the action as a possibility rather than a completed success.
Had to reports necessity, not whether the restart succeeded.
Managed to explicitly reports successful completion, often after difficulty.

explanation: 'Could' is the usual reported form of 'can' when referring to ability at that past time.

rationales.must: 'Must' changes an ability into a requirement or conclusion.
rationales.would: 'Would' can report willingness or a future action, but it does not preserve the stated ability.
rationales.should: 'Should' changes the statement into advice or expectation.
rationales.could: 'Could' is the usual reported form of 'can' when referring to ability at that past time.

rationales.drive: Unlike should, ought normally needs to before its following verb.
rationales.to driving: Use the basic form drive after ought to.
rationales.driven: A past participle alone cannot follow ought; use ought to drive.

sentence: 'The courier is supposed to collect the parcel at three.'

options: The courier collected the parcel before three.
The arrangement says collection should happen at three.
The courier is able to lift the parcel at three.
The courier would prefer a three o'clock collection.
answer: The arrangement says collection should happen at three.
focusKey: coverage-modals-b1-1969:Be supposed to for an arrangement
explanation: Be supposed to can refer to an agreed plan or an expected duty; it does not confirm performance.

rationales.The courier collected the parcel before: Is supposed to describes the arrangement, not a completed collection.
rationales.The arrangement says collection should h: Be supposed to can refer to an agreed plan or an expected duty; it does not confirm performance.
rationales.The courier is able to lift the parcel a: Ability to lift is different from an arrangement to collect.
rationales.The courier would prefer a three o'clock: The sentence reports what is arranged, not the courier's preference.

rationales.didn't need to: This removes a need to access the archive, not permission.
rationales.wasn't allowed to: Wasn't allowed to directly identifies permission as the missing condition.
rationales.wasn't willing to: This would mean you refused or did not want to enter, not that approval was missing.

rationales.must not: Must not gives a negative rule or conclusion, not the expected completion time.
rationales.has to: Has to would make four a necessary deadline, which is not what the technician is estimating.
rationales.should: Should can express an expected result based on what normally happens or on current information.

I'd rather get up at five.
answer: I'm used to getting up at five.

explanation: Be used to + -ing means an activity is familiar or normal to you.

Be used to + -ing means an activity is familiar or normal to you.
Used to + basic verb describes a former habit rather than present familiarity.
Ought to recommends the action, not how familiar it feels.

answer: I'd rather walk than take a taxi.

explanation: Would rather + verb + than states a preference between two available actions.

Would rather + verb + than states a preference between two available actions.

Might describes a possible choice without directly stating a preference.

rationales.Heavy traffic occurs on this road at som: 'Can' can describe an occasional or typical possibility, such as summer traffic.

Needn't means there is no necessity to print; printing is not thereby forbidden.

The meetings were possible only under an unstated condition.
answer: Meeting on Fridays was a repeated past activity.
explanation: 'Would' can describe repeated actions within an established past period.

rationales.Meeting on Fridays was a repeated past a: 'Would' can describe repeated actions within an established past period.
rationales.The speaker is making a polite request f: This statement recounts what happened; it is not a request addressed to someone.
rationales.The meetings were possible only under an: No hypothetical condition is needed here because 'would' describes an actual past routine.
